semantically_equivalent_models.justification: 'Chronosymbolic framework' and 'Chronosymbolic learning' both revolve around the integration of temporal and symbolic learning paradigms. The term 'learning' can often be interchanged with 'framework' when discussing theoretical models or approaches in the context of machine learning, which makes them semantically equivalent.

parent_models.justification: Markovian models represent a broad class of models that deal with state space and probabilistic transitions over time, which relates them as a parent category to specific temporal learning frameworks like the chronosymbolic framework.

Polynomial dynamical systems are broad mathematical frameworks that can underpin various temporal models, and can encompass methods such as the chronosymbolic framework which integrates time dynamics in learning.

closest_parent_model.justification: Markovian models specifically focus on time-dependent state transitions and probabilistic modeling, which aligns closely with the temporal aspects of the chronosymbolic framework, making them the closest parent in terms of semantic meaning.

child_models.justification: Being part of the same conceptual domain, chronosymbolic learning is a specific instance or implementation of the more theoretical chronosymbolic framework.

closest_child_model.justification: As the only semantically equivalent model found that also acts as a child implementation, chronosymbolic learning serves as the closest child model to the chronosymbolic framework.

closest_sibling_model.justification: The Koopman-based dynamics model is focused on temporal dynamics analysis, directly aligning with the time-dependent, dynamic-oriented nature of the chronosymbolic framework, more so than the others.
